name: Talkspace Psychiatry
one_liner: Psychiatry and medication management from the largest online therapy platform, with most insurance copays at $0.
short_description: Talkspace Psychiatry offers psychiatric evaluations and medication management through licensed psychiatrists and psychiatric NPs, with insurance billing and low copays.
long_description: Talkspace Psychiatry is the medication management service from Talkspace, one of the largest online therapy platforms in the United States. Available to adults 18 and older, Talkspace Psychiatry provides psychiatric evaluations and ongoing medication management through licensed psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners. The platform accepts major insurance plans including Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Optum, BCBS, and TRICARE, with most insured members paying $0 copay. Without insurance, initial evaluations cost $299 and follow-ups $175. Talkspace requires visits at least every 3 months for prescription refills. Unlike some competitors, Talkspace cannot prescribe controlled substances including ADHD stimulants or benzodiazepines. In 2026, Talkspace introduced an AI mental health support tool called Tee ($19.99/month).

faqs.a: No, Talkspace clinicians cannot prescribe controlled substances including stimulants for ADHD or benzodiazepines. If your evaluation determines these are needed, you must transfer care to another provider.

faqs.q: How much does Talkspace Psychiatry cost?
faqs.a: With insurance, most patients pay $0-30 copay. Without insurance, initial evaluations cost $299 and follow-ups $175. Talkspace accepts Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Optum, BCBS, and TRICARE.

faqs.q: How often do I need appointments for refills?
faqs.a: Talkspace requires that you meet with your psychiatric provider at least every 3 months to receive prescription refills. Some providers may require more frequent visits based on your needs.

faqs.q: Is Talkspace Psychiatry for adults only?
faqs.a: Yes, Talkspace Psychiatry is only available for individuals 18 and older. Children and teens are not able to use the psychiatry services.
